Commentary.Commentary: 216 seems like a modest total but with the pitch turning as it is, it might prove to be enough. Dew, if it does come, might play a role. Join us back in a while for the run chase.

The pitch is turning square and the spinners did decently, till the onslaught came about from Rashid and Asghar. 32 runs came in the last 2 overs, which could be telling on such pitches. Andy McBrine was the pick of the lot with his 1/30 in 10 overs.

Catches win you matches is a cliche. Ireland dropped not one, not two but as many as 4 catches. Surely they could have restricted Afghanistan below 200 or even 150. Two of those catches were of Asghar himself.

Yet another same story which has enveloped in the last few games. Afghanistan top order stutters, then Ireland get on top, only to see the middle order fight back. Today, Asghar Afghan managed to bat through till the end (almost) and found an able partner again in Nabi and later, Rashid. The hosts were 50/4 at one stage but Ireland simply could not press the advantage.

Wow. We have finished 15 minutes before the scheduled innings break. Well, if in a 50-over inning, 80 percent of the overs are bowled by spin, you would expect that, wouldn't you? Just 11 overs bowled by seam by Ireland. Ouch. My fingers...
This is just inside the line! Full and outside off, Khan lets it go and the ball just about kisses the wide line! AFGHANISTAN FINISH ON 216/6!

SAFE BUT A WIDE BALL. Rashid jumps down the track and the bowler throws it very wide outside off. It is so wide that Khan cannot reach it and lets it go. He then tries to get back and then the keeper whips the bails off. The stumping appeal is referred upstairs but replays show that the bat came down before the bails were dislodged.
Stumped off a wide? No one is celebrating. No one is going anywhere. Referred upstairs...

SIX! SMASH! Oh yeah... Rashid the slogger. Full and outside off, Khan comes down the track and sends it sailing over long off!
Comes down the track and swats it towards long off who takes his own sweet time in returning the ball. Two runs taken.

Oh dear... an interruption. Right in the middle of the final over. Asghar is not happy with his hamstring. The physio is out in the middle.

SIX! STUPENDOUS! Oh hello!!!!! This is a message to the selectors, not Ireland. Dropped me, did yeah? Here is my response. What a way to kickstart proceedings. Really kickstarted. A length ball, around middle and Shahzad is already halfway down the track! Gets to the pitch of the ball and swings it miles over mid-wicket!
The players are out in the middle. Mohammad Shahzad and Javed Ahmadi will open for Afghanistan. Tim Murtagh will start off proceedings with the first new ball to Shahzad. Here we go...

Afghanistan playing XI - Not surprisingly, Mohammad Shahzad is back for Afghanistan. An interesting name crops up as well - ZAHIR KHAN - Touted to be a chinaman, who is making his international debut. There are as many as 5 changes. Even the captain himself did not remember who came in and who went out. Er... guess we shall focus more on the game then?
Ireland playing XI - The visitors have gone in with the same playing XI as on Friday, citing their confidence.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. William Porterfield calls Heads and Heads it is. IRELAND OPT TO CHASE.
WEATHER - It is another clear day in Dehradun with the sun shining brightly as ever. No forecast of rain today.

The home side was brilliant with the ball in the previous game but knowing the stern man that Asghar Afghan is, he will certainly not be happy on the batting front. In all the matches so far, including the T20Is, the Afghan top order has struggled to fire, something which they are not accustomed to. Today is one final chance to set that right, before they embark on their World Cup year.

If there was a feeling that Ireland would bounce back following their win in the third ODI, everything was put to rest in the next. They were thoroughly humbled on Friday, with the result that they cannot win the series, albeit there is a chance to have it squared. Will Afghanistan allow them to do that though? Hello and a warm welcome to the fifth and final ODI between Afghanistan and Ireland in Dehradun.
